links.outcome: Report summarization F1 and expert-rated quality, specialized LLM versus general-purpose GPT-4o on same data
links.effect: LLM-RadSum median F1 0.58 vs GPT-4o 0.30 (P<.001); 81.5% (1467/1800) LLM-RadSum outputs met standards vs at least 27.8% (501/1800) GPT-4o outputs needing adjustment.
links.quote: Overall, LLM-RadSum achieved a higher median F1 score for report summarization compared with GPT-4o (0.58 [IQR: 0.44-0.77] vs 0.30 [IQR: 0.23-0.37]; P < .001); superior performance from LLM-RadSum was observed across anatomic regions, modalities, sexes, ages, and impression lengths (all P < .001).

links.outcome: Performance drop from internal to external test sets of other hospitals
links.effect: LLM-RadSum median F1 0.75 on internal test set versus 0.44 on external test set from four other hospitals.
links.quote: The developed LLM-RadSum achieved median F1 scores for report summarization of 0.75 and 0.44 on the internal and external test sets and 0.58 on the human evaluation set (n = 1800).

unlisted_practices: Domain-specific fine-tuning of an LLM on large radiology report corpus for summarization

screen.reason: Empirical study comparing a specialized LLM (LLM-RadSum) against GPT-4o for radiology report summarization using retrospective data and human expert evaluation, but it evaluates model performance rather than testing an organizational deployment practice or safeguard.
